scope: Archive entry validation/extraction, digest/mode/metadata checks, hostile archive risks, release asset selection

findings.title: verifyArchive accepts non-regular archive members and executes an out-of-tree symlink target
findings.evidence: archiveListing (126) parses only tar -tzf names; stat() at 187 follows symlinks; run([binary,'--version']) at 232 and [binary,'--help'] at 237 execute whatever the path resolves to. Reproduced: archive with swarmforge -> /tmp/sf-probe/outside/swarmforge plus matching SHA256SUMS/metadata returned VERIFIED_OK (exit 0), and the out-of-tree target appended OUTSIDE-EXEC to a marker file twice while verification ran.
findings.reproduction: tar member 'swarmforge' of type symlink to an out-of-tree 0755 file; SHA256SUMS/metadata computed over the link target; bun -e "verifyArchive({archivePath, expectedVersion:'0.1.0'})" exits 0. Probes /tmp/sf-probe/hostile.tar.gz, probe1.ts, probe5.ts (log: .swarmforge/logs/review-45-archive-verification.log).
findings.recommendation: Before extraction, reject any member whose tar type is not a regular file; after extraction assert lstat().isFile() for every expected path and never stat/exec through a link. Keep GNU tar's traversal rejection as defence in depth.

findings.title: Permission check masks setuid/setgid/sticky bits, certifying a setuid-root binary as 0755
findings.evidence: (await stat(binary)).mode & 0o777 strips 0o4000/0o2000/0o1000 before comparing to 0o755; metadata mode at 224 is a string comparison against the literal '0755'. Reproduced: 4755 archive verified OK (SETUID_ARCHIVE_VERIFIED), extracted file is -rwsr-xr-x while metadata.executable.mode says 0755.
findings.reproduction: Package a member with mode 4755 plus self-consistent SHA256SUMS/metadata; verifyArchive returns success and `stat -c %a` on the extracted tree shows 4755.
findings.recommendation: Compare the full mode (mode & 0o7777) to 0o755 and reject any archive whose recorded member mode carries setuid/setgid/sticky.

findings.title: Whitespace-only archive members are dropped, so the exact three-file listing check can be bypassed
findings.evidence: Names are .trim()ed then filtered to length > 0 before comparison at 170. Reproduced: archive with the three expected members plus a member named '  ' extracted successfully and verified, returning files=[SHA256SUMS, metadata-0.1.0.json, swarmforge].
findings.reproduction: Add a fourth tar member whose name is two spaces; verifyArchive still reports the archive as containing exactly the expected files.
findings.recommendation: Normalize names without trimming to empty and explicitly reject any member whose normalized name is empty instead of filtering it away.

findings.title: prepareReleaseAssets never checks the loose SHA256SUMS/metadata against the verified archive, and findFile selection is readdir-ordered and recursive
findings.evidence: findFile (356) returns the first name match at any depth. Reproduced: a directory holding a valid archive plus an all-zero-digest SHA256SUMS and a 1-byte metadata-0.1.0.json returned PREPARED_OK with all three listed as release assets; a second probe selected nested/SHA256SUMS over the flat layout. The draft job then uploads those loose files (release.yml:153-159).
findings.reproduction: Build an asset directory from a valid archive and replace the standalone SHA256SUMS/metadata with self-inconsistent content; prepareReleaseAssets succeeds and reports them as the assets to publish.
findings.recommendation: Digest-compare the loose SHA256SUMS and metadata JSON against the copies extracted from the verified archive and reject any mismatch; restrict findFile to the flat download-artifact layout with deterministic ordering and duplicate rejection.
